conviction_note: This is Airtel Money's first results since its 9 October 2026 IPO at 196p. Q1 is already public through the prospectus's June financial statements, and Q2 was described as 'in line' on 23 September against FY27 targets set by the company. There is no sell-side consensus because research is blacked out until after 19 November, and the guide is not expected to move. So the release adds Q2 detail, a reiteration of the targets and the first interim dividend. The findings sum to +0.6, all small positives inside the guide. abs_move is 5.5: the pre-released base of about 3%, raised for a first print as a listed company with an 11% free float and no published research. p_up is 54, a lean that rests on proxies, so expected_move = 0.08 x 5.5 = +0.44.

already_public.what: FY27 targets: constant-currency revenue growth in the mid-20%s; underlying EBITDA margin to moderate by up to ~2pp from FY26 (~50%); capex 3-4% of revenue; dividend policy of at least 80% of attributable net profit, paid semi-annually
Current trading: 'Since 1 July 2026, the Group has continued to trade in line with the Directors' expectations ... remains on track to deliver results in line with the outlook and near-term targets'
Q1 FY27 standalone (3 months to 30 June 2026): revenue $399m vs $289m; operating profit $184m vs $144m; profit $111m vs $90m (owners $104m vs $85m)
Parent's Q1: mobile money revenue +25.8% constant currency, +38.9% reported; segment EBITDA margin 49.1%, down 363bps because intra-group agreements were renegotiated

new_in_release.expect: Q2 numbers are new, but they were described as in line on 23 Sep. Expect H1 constant-currency revenue growth in the mid-20%s and reported growth in the 30s on FX. Inside the guide; slight upside on margin because Q1 standalone EBITDA ran at about 50% against a guide that allows about 48%.
The FY27 targets are most likely reiterated. A raise or cut is unlikely five weeks after the prospectus. Unknown either way.

First interim dividend, expected at 80% or more of H1 attributable profit. On Q1 owners' profit of $104m doubled, that is roughly 6 US cents (~4.6p) a share. This is an inference, not a company number. A dividend below 80% or deferred would read negative.
unknown; no external borrowings per the investment case
Possible one-off IPO costs in H1. They sit below underlying EBITDA and the guide excludes them.

bar: The company's own FY27 targets in the ITF of 23 Sep 2026: constant-currency revenue growth in the mid-20%s, underlying EBITDA margin down by up to ~2pp from ~50%. Source: https://cdn-webportal.airtelstream.net/website/airtel-money/investor-website/assets/pdf/ipo-documents/IPO_Intention+to+Float+Announcement.pdf. There is no sell-side consensus: the IR site says coverage starts 'after Nov 19, 2026' (https://www.airtelmoney.com/analysts-and-consensus).
session_check: bmo. The issuer's Notice of Results (RNS, 21 Oct 2026, 14:02) says the half-year results come on Monday 26 October 2026 and that management hosts a webcast 'on the day of results at 12:00 GMT'. The release therefore lands before midday, and the issuer's earlier RNS went out at 07:00. The exact release time is not stated, so this is an inference without a timestamp. https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/airtel-mobile-commerce-n-v---amc/notice-of-results/9834711
positioning_check: The FCA aggregated register (as of 2026-10-21) has no position at or above 0.5%. That is a truncated zero on a name listed two weeks ago, not evidence that nobody is short; anchor_covered is false, so priced_lean is the run-up. The visible positioning is the stabilising manager. Citi bought 23,046,027 shares between 9 and 15 Oct, against an over-allotment of up to 27,000,000, at 174.06-196.00p (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/airtel-mobile-commerce-n-v---amc/stabilisation-notice/9828068, 2026-10-16). That leaves at most about 4m shares of stabilisation capacity, and the period can run to about 8 Nov.

findings.finding: H1 should land inside the FY27 targets. Q1 standalone revenue was $399m (+38%) at an EBITDA margin of about 50% (operating profit $184m plus D&A $17m), above the guide's allowance of up to 2pp margin moderation, and the company said on 23 Sep that trading since 1 July was in line.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None. This is the first results release since listing; the history has 0 events.
findings.why_not_priced: It mostly is: Q1 and the 'in line' statement were in the prospectus. What is not priced is the Q2 detail, which no analyst can preview because research is blacked out until after 19 Nov. Had the market priced a beat, the stock would not sit 9.6% below the 196p offer after falling 8.4% from its 16 Oct high (193.56p to 177.2p).
findings.independence: The parent's Q1 segment data shows mobile money +25.8% cc, consistent with the mid-20%s target: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/airtel-africa--aaf/q1-results/9682984

findings.finding: The release will carry the first interim dividend under a policy of at least 80% of attributable net profit paid semi-annually. On Q1 owners' profit of $104m that implies about 6 US cents (~4.6p) a share for H1, about 2.6% of the share price for one half-year.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None; this is the first dividend as a listed company.
findings.why_not_priced: The policy is public. The first declared amount, and whether it is struck on a full half-year at 80% or more, is not. A stock trading below offer with no research is not discounting a confirmed ~5% annualised yield; if it were, the post-IPO slide would have stopped at the offer price.

findings.finding: Two features of the positioning. The stabilising manager has at most about 4m shares of over-allotment cover left (23.05m of up to 27m bought by 15 Oct), and stabilisation can run to about 8 Nov, so some bid support exists on the day. Sell-side research is blacked out until after 19 Nov, so the release is the first new company information since the IPO for an 11% free float that is already below offer.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None for this name. Stabilisation bought 18.5m shares on day one at 184-196p and only 0.2-2.5m a day after that.
findings.why_not_priced: The remaining stabilisation capacity is a small, inferred cushion; nobody has disclosed purchases after 15 Oct. This is mainly a reason the move is larger rather than a direction, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Research blackout stated on the issuer's IR site: https://www.airtelmoney.com/analysts-and-consensus

outside_window.finding: Initiation of sell-side research coverage 'expected after Nov 19, 2026' (end of the IPO research blackout)
Stabilisation period ends no later than 30 calendar days after conditional dealings began on 9 Oct (about 8 Nov); an end-of-stabilisation notice will follow
Parent Airtel Africa's own H1 results, which carry the mobile money segment; the date is not yet announced (the prior year was 28 Oct)

searched_and_found_nothing: Sell-side consensus or analyst previews: none exist because of the research blackout to after 19 Nov (issuer IR page).

News explaining the 5-day fall of 7.1%: only coverage of the debut below offer and a telecoms selloff after SpaceX's spectrum purchase (thepaypers, zawya, billionaires.africa). Nothing company-specific.
FTSE UK index inclusion: the company expects to be eligible, but no fast-entry or review date falls inside the window.
Airtel Africa notice of H1 results: none posted on Investegate as of 2026-10-23.
Prospectus PDF (11MB): eu_pdftext.py extracted mostly unreadable subset-font text, so no H1 FY26 comparative could be read. The ITF and June 2026 statements were readable.
Sharecast, Proactive and Investors' Chronicle are known 403s and were not retried.
baseline_tension: The findings lean mildly positive, against a small negative priced_lean (-0.108) and a -7.1% 5-day run-up. They are weak proxies inside the guide, so they move p_up only to 54 and do not fight the tape hard.
language_note: The domestic sources (the RNS mirror on Investegate and the issuer's own IR pages) carried the 16 Oct stabilisation notice showing 23.05m of 27m over-allotment shares bought, the 12:00 GMT webcast that settles the session, and the research blackout to after 19 Nov. None of this appeared in the English wire coverage, which covered only the debut below offer.
lessons_applied: 'A finding about a number the market has already been told is worth 0': the H1-inside-guide finding was cut from +0.3 to +0.1, because Q1 and the 'in line' Q2 statement are public.

'You were right about the number and too small about the move' and 'understatement is the systematic error': abs_move raised from 4.5 to 5.5 for a first print as a listed company with no research and an 11% free float, even though the period is partly pre-released.
The truncated-zero rule: positioning_check now says the FCA zero is the 0.5% floor on a new listing, not evidence of no shorts.
